title: The Bjerknes feedback in the tropical Atlantic in CMIP5 models
problem: State-of-the-art climate models perform poorly in simulating tropical Atlantic climate, and this study investigates whether these biases are caused by an inaccurate representation of the Bjerknes feedback, particularly the flawed coupling between subsurface ocean heat content and sea surface temperature.
method: This study investigates the Bjerknes feedback in CMIP5 models by subdividing it into three components and using monthly correlation analysis to compare the resulting spatial patterns with reanalysis data via pattern correlation, thereby diagnosing model biases in the tropical Atlantic.
task: The task is to investigate the Bjerknes feedback in the tropical Atlantic by analyzing it in reanalysis data and comparing the findings to CMIP5 model outputs to evaluate model performance and identify biases in simulating this key air-sea interaction mechanism.
innovation: This paper provides a detailed component-wise analysis of the Bjerknes feedback in CMIP5 models, pinpointing the flawed simulation of the local sea surface temperature response to subsurface ocean heat content as the primary source of error in representing tropical Atlantic climate variability.

Abstract Coupled state-of-the-art general circulation models still perform relatively poorly in simulating tropical Atlantic (TA) climate. To investigate whether lack of air-sea interaction might be responsible for their biases, we investigate the Bjerknes feedback (BF) in the TA, the driver of the dominant interannual variability in that region.

A prerequsite of simulating TA climate correctly is that the mechanisms that govern TA climate and its variability are well represented in the models. While the large annual cycle causes most of the SST variablity in the TA, two other leading modes of interannual to decadal variability have been identified: the zonal and the meridional mode.
